products.name: Madagascar Vanilla
products.format: Core EDP · Travel size · Mini charm · Balm
products.brief:
**Recorded notes source:** Recorded label/website agreement.

**Notes:** Jasmine/Gardenia/Croissant → Whipped Cream/Brown Sugar/Tonka → Madagascar Vanilla/Coconut

**Recorded brand description:** “This sophisticated scent combines creamy Coconut, crisp Croissant, and warm Madagascar Vanilla for an utterly addictive island escape. The result is a deliciously exotic yet subtly sweet fragrance that is sure to captivate and delight. Enjoy a tropical getaway with each spritz of this sensuous and inviting aroma.”

**Source status / cautions:** Actual product reference was supplied in this chat. No note conflict recorded here.

**Creative history / options:** Earlier Escape reading and new comparative board: Somewhere Else / Nothing Urgent / Soft Landing. Somewhere Else was selected for an initial test; later clarification established the comparative board as the intended territory deliverable. No blanket approval of every tile.

**Previously recorded reference/history paths:** `products/Madagascar_Vanilla.webp`, `_flat_lay.webp`. Check the actual files before use.
products.source: fragrance-briefs.md · updated 2026-11-04; recorded evidence, not freshly verified

products.name: Vanilla Crème
products.format: Core EDP · Travel size · Mini charm
products.brief:
**Recorded notes source:** Label and website records.

**Notes:** Crème → Almond (website adds Milk) → Creamy Vanilla/Skin Musk/Tonka

**Recorded brand description:** “This soft, creamy vanilla fragrance is like wearing a warm, powdery, fluffy cloud. It's a 10/10 for anyone who wants to smell like a dream!”

**Source status / cautions:** Minor source wording variance retained; not silently normalized. Distinguish EDP from similarly named oil.

**Creative history / options:** Cloud/stone route overlapped with Vanilla Era. The prior round-2 custard route was preferred in that test. Comfort/Stillness is a creative reading, not a required food scene.
products.source: fragrance-briefs.md · updated 2026-11-04; recorded evidence, not freshly verified

products.name: Vanilla Era
products.format: Core EDP · Travel size · Mini charm
products.brief:
**Recorded notes source:** Recorded label/reference and brand description.

**Notes:** Vanilla Orchid/Sugar → Jasmine Blossom/White Flowers → Tonka/Agarwood/Vanilla

**Recorded brand description:** “A scent that feels like second skin—soft, warm, and effortlessly seductive. Creamy sugary vanilla bean melts into delicate white florals, creating an intoxicating sweetness that lingers like a secret only you know. Velvety Agar wood and Tonka wrap around you, leaving a trail that feels both comforting and captivating. Vanilla Era is not just a fragrance—it's an experience: timeless, luxurious, and impossible to forget.”

**Source status / cautions:** “Second skin” and “all-day” are brand language, not measured low projection or proof of universal occasion fit.

**Creative history / options:** Presence/Second Skin, fabric/proximity; historical generated interpretation. Hard surfaces or glossy elements are not categorically forbidden.

**Previously recorded reference/history paths:** `products/Vanilla_Era.jpg`. Check the actual files before use.
products.source: fragrance-briefs.md · updated 2026-11-04; recorded evidence, not freshly verified

products.name: Bourbon Vanilla
products.format: Core EDP · Travel size · Mini charm
products.brief:
**Recorded notes source:** Recorded label/website sources.

**Notes:** Vanilla Orchid/Jasmine → Brown Sugar/Tonka → Amber/Amberwood/Musk/Patchouli

**Recorded brand description:** “An oriental blend of Madagascar vanilla orchid, Brazilian Tonka, musk, amber, patchouli and brown sugar. It has beautifully balanced oriental notes of musk, amber, patchouli and brown sugar from the distinguished wood base of this utterly sublime scent.”

**Source status / cautions:** Bourbon vanilla is geographic terminology, not evidence of whiskey. No alcohol accord is established by the supplied description. Box #22 / bottle #20 discrepancy remains recorded.

**Creative history / options:** Vanilla warmth/woody-amber depth is a candidate reading. The earlier barrel/bar image remains a historical experiment with a corrected name-based rationale, not a preferred route.

**Previously recorded reference/history paths:** `creative-territory-method.md`, `bourbon-vanilla-barrel.png`, `products/Bourbon_Vanilla.jpg`. Check the actual files before use.

products.name: Tipsy
products.format: Core EDP · Travel size · Mini charm
products.brief:
**Recorded notes source:** Label record and website description.

**Notes:** Cinnamon/Cardamom/Ginger → Praline/Candied Fruits/White Flowers → Coffee/Vanilla/Tonka/Benzoin/Musk

**Recorded brand description:** “Spicy, sweet, and just a little bit risky—Tipsy is like a cozy night out that you can wear! Cinnamon, praline, and a touch of coffee create a scent that's bold, addictive, and made to make people lean in a little closer. Go ahead, get Tipsy!”

**Source status / cautions:** The recorded description spans nights out and evenings in; no compulsory time/place slot.

**Creative history / options:** Warm spice, coffee or dessert cocktail, knit texture; proposals, not evidence of an alcohol accord.

prompts.text:
Create ONE landscape 3:2 high-resolution editorial comparative CREATIVE TERRITORY MOODBOARD for Go Natural Caramel Latte. INPUT IMAGE is exact product identity reference ONLY, not graphic layout or photographic style. Three equal columns, elegant warm ivory paper background, restrained dark espresso serif typography with quiet sans labels, contemporary art-directed collage spacing and thin gutters. Rich imaginative sensory routes, sophisticated BELIEVABLE photographic references, not generic AI luxury. Full-width header 'Go Natural' and large 'Caramel Latte', small 'CREATIVE TERRITORY EXPLORATION', concise source-grounded line 'Creamy vanilla, milk, honey and caramel.' Footer 'SCENT CUES: Caramel · Milk · Honey · White flowers · Vanilla · Musk'. Small bottom note 'Concept studies, not finished campaigns'. No longevity claim, no coffee note claim.

Actual collected product description: creamy lactonic vanilla ice cream drenched in honey and caramel; playful 'you will smell edible'. Notes Caramel/Milk -> Honey/White Flowers -> Vanilla/Musk. Explore freely through sensory food, place/ritual, wearer/presence, combining evocative associations. No need to allocate light temperature or exclusively own materials; lighting serves ideas. All three allow nuanced inviting warmth without uniform orange grading, glossy syrup overload or forced cold counterpoint.

Product lock: faithful reference cylindrical tall clear glass bottle, thick clear base, near-clear very pale warm champagne liquid, polished gold spherical cap, off-white label exact black Go Natural serif, fine brown Caramel Latte cursive, small actual printed #10 on bottle. Preserve silhouette/label layout. Remove cork tube packaging, do not copy cork reflection as a physical cap marking, no redesign. Product study once per column with comparable modest prominence; don't paste same giant bottle in foreground everywhere. Four to six diverse separate image tiles in each column exploring world, ingredients, light, gesture, texture.

COLUMN 1 title 'The First Spoonful' subtitle 'Anticipation becomes pleasure.'
Food/sensation route: tactile creamy lactonic richness grounded in vanilla ice cream, milk, honey and caramel. Main macro editorial photograph a silver spoon lifting ONE small soft curl of vanilla ice cream, modest thin caramel ribbon folds back onto it, natural tiny ice crystals and vanilla flecks, melting edge, physically plausible. Off-white ceramic glimpse, muted apricot field. Supporting tiles: thick cream folding in a small jug, fine honey thread catching directional daylight, vanilla pod and delicate white blossom, small faithful bottle on matte pale peach surface alongside ONE minimal caramel/cream cue. Vary scale and composition with breathing room; sensual appetite rather than giant candy sculpture. Broad directional window light creates delicious creamy rounded volume, delicate shadows and controlled honey glint, creamy neutral whites no orange syrup flood. Palette buttercream, pale apricot, caramel, warm ivory, espresso accent. KEY ELEMENTS 'Creamy folds · Slow melt' / 'Anticipation · Small indulgence'.

COLUMN 2 title 'Your Usual, Upgraded' subtitle 'An everyday ritual worth lingering over.'
Place/ritual route: stylish contemporary Egyptian urban café atmosphere without invented signage or tourist cues; warm oak, matte green ceramic, subtle brass detail and inviting daylight. Main candid editorial adult woman in a rich green casual shirt at a small cafe window counter, pausing mid-conversation with genuine relaxed expression; a modest milk-based latte cup on counter, small faithful bottle near her bag. Latte is a cultural association, NOT an asserted coffee ingredient. No barista theatrics or splashes. Supporting tiles: hand wrapping naturally around muted green ceramic, a soft milk swirl seen close with only a little caramel color, brushed brass/wood detail, warm daylight passing across a sleeve and tabletop, small flower reference optional. Realistic lived-in specifics, no generic books/newspapers or unrelated prop pile. Light is believable warm-neutral side daylight with gentle falloff, natural skin and shadows, background not drowned in golden haze. Palette bottle green, honey oak, cream, soft brass, cocoa. KEY ELEMENTS 'Daily pleasure · Personal ritual' / 'Warm daylight · Contemporary café'.

COLUMN 3 title 'Sweet on You' subtitle 'A little sweetness, worn with personality.'
Wearer/presence route inspired by playful edible copy, not a guaranteed reaction from others. Main candid adult woman wearing a soft raspberry/coral knit cardigan over cream shirt, amused half smile and relaxed wrist/hand near collar, a personal getting-ready mirror moment with tangible human personality. Close enough for skin/fabric texture, not stock seduction or symmetrical almost-kissing couple. Small faithful bottle on dressing shelf partly in shot. Supporting distinct tiles: hand gently smoothing sleeve with tactile knit, playful raspberry lipstick mark on an unbranded cream cup as a personal trace (subtle not giant graphic), satin-smooth milk-white material and thin honey-colored translucent detail juxtaposed, small vanilla/white flowers cue. Food associations inform creamy texture and inviting warmth without turning woman into dessert. Shaped soft warm-neutral light flatters while retaining natural pores, depth under chin and fabric creases, realistic reflections and restrained retouching. Raspberry/coral highlights, warm skin, cream and brown depth, no obligatory beige or dark noir. Palette muted raspberry, rose clay, warm ivory, honey, deep cocoa. KEY ELEMENTS 'Playful presence · Creamy softness' / 'Personal gesture · Inviting warmth'.

Board typography should be expertly aligned and fully readable, titles fit columns, palette swatches 5 each under collages, key elements short. Images should have specific editorial photography, plausible materials and subtle natural variation, not hyperglossy commercial CGI, oversize ingredients, floating products, randomly glowing objects or repeated cream fabric across every tile. Preserve variety and sensory pleasure. Some highlights and color are welcome when purposeful. Keep all source ingredients accurate: no added coffee in scent footer, no whiskey, no fake amber crystal, no extravagant performance copy. Make product reference identity faithful and each route compelling rather than merely orderly.

prompts.text:
Create ONE refined landscape 3:2 creative territory exploration MOODBOARD for Go Natural Tipsy. Input 1 is exact product identity, input 2 is graphic layout precedent ONLY, not lighting or composition to imitate. Rebuild photographic collages thoughtfully. Preserve elegant cream paper editorial design, black serif text, full width header, three equal territory columns, palette swatches/key elements, fragrance DNA footer. Three complete visual worlds grounded in: "Spicy, sweet, and just a little bit risky—Tipsy is like a cozy night out that you can wear! Cinnamon, praline, and a touch of coffee create a scent that's bold, addictive, and made to make people lean in a little closer." Warmth and invitation are central. Lighting must support each idea, not demonstrate arbitrary warm/cool contrasts. No obligatory cold blue or teal. No uniformly orange/golden glaze either: natural color, shaped light, tasteful depth.

Product lock whenever bottle appears: input 1 straight cylindrical transparent glass, thick clear base, very pale champagne blush liquid, polished pale gold spherical cap, white label exact black Go Natural serif and fine orange-brown Tipsy script, EAU DE PARFUM. Copy actual shape/proportions/artwork closely. No cork packaging, no reflected cork mark on cap, no dark coffee liquid. Use modest product-context studies within each varied collage, not three identical giant bottles composited in front of imagery.

HEADER exact 'Go Natural' / 'Fragrance Collection', large 'Tipsy', small 'CREATIVE TERRITORY EXPLORATION', line 'Spicy, sweet, and just a little bit risky.'

COLUMN 1 TERRITORY 01 / 'Lean Closer' / subtitle 'The warmth between us.'
Visual idea: genuine ease and attraction in an intimate evening. Main atmosphere tile: two adult friends/lovers in an elegant small booth naturally leaning closer to hear a whispered aside, subtle spontaneous smile/laughter, relaxed shoulders, believable fully clothed posture and unposed hands resting naturally. Medium editorial crop, no stiff symmetrical almost-touching fingers or mannequin seduction. Warm directional soft-edged side light wraps their faces and shared space, warm-neutral skin, shadow on far cheeks creates depth; shadows remain rich plum/brown, no blue cast. Restrained practical light in background only. Realistic texture and natural highlight rolloff, no orange skin, waxy retouch or bloom. Burgundy cloth and deep espresso surroundings, gentle bronze accents. Supporting separate tiles: expressive candid smile/cheek close-up, hand relaxed against textured dark sleeve, softly illuminated cinnamon/vanilla macro with natural scale, small accurate product on dark wood with warm side reflection. Palette burgundy, espresso, soft bronze, warm skin rose, ivory. KEY ELEMENTS 'Shared warmth · Candid closeness' / 'Soft side light · Natural skin'.

COLUMN 2 TERRITORY 02 / 'Sweet Trouble' / subtitle 'Sweetness with a mischievous edge.'
Visual idea playful spice and small transgression, lively still-life rather than an enormous surreal object. Main still-life bottle on matte oxblood-red tabletop with a few SMALL real cinnamon quills, a modest snapped praline piece whose brittle edge catches light and a few coffee beans; unexpected diagonal framing and an accurately rendered cropped adult hand entering to take the tiny praline piece, a playful inviting moment. Maintain fragrance hierarchy; no giant bark/driftwood, towering caramel sculpture, floods of syrup, chocolate advert. Crisp directional warm-neutral raking light reveals rough cinnamon and brittle praline, clean defined shadows convey snap/energy. Light is not cold or harsh for its own sake. Red/oxblood and toasted brown color, small peach/candied accent. Separate reference tiles show real cinnamon quill cross-section, crushed praline crumb texture, coffee beans in directional light, muted candied orange zest detail, curved hand gesture. Palette oxblood, cinnamon brown, burnt coral, muted caramel, parchment. KEY ELEMENTS 'Playful gesture · Spiced texture' / 'Crisp light · A little indulgence'.

COLUMN 3 TERRITORY 03 / 'Stay a Little Longer' / subtitle 'The evening is not over yet.'
Visual idea lingering after-dinner conversation, cozy but sociable and alive, not abandoned furniture or bedtime. Main atmosphere tile: adult person relaxed sideways on a deep upholstered lounge seat, smiling toward an off-frame companion, a casual sleeve pushed back and natural resting hand; small table nearby with bottle and a small espresso cup, after-hours intimate lounge. Main image emphasizes lived human presence and the ongoing moment, not a large chair or blanket. Warm table-lamp light falls gently on wrist, sleeve and tabletop, background progressively softer/dimmer, soft shadows and restrained neutral ambient fill. Natural brown/olive shadows rather than blue night-light requirement. Small highlights on coffee cup/glass, tactile matte fabric. No mountain of fluffy knit, no showroom interior. Supporting separate tiles: warm pool of light on wood, softly rumpled fine fabric, espresso crema small macro, tonka/vanilla texture, candid leaning-back gesture. Palette deep olive, cocoa, tobacco tan, soft warm grey, cream. KEY ELEMENTS 'Lingering conversation · Easy comfort' / 'Gentle falloff · Coffee warmth'.

Make each column an exploratory collage with varying crops/scales and around 5 reference tiles, not a single finished campaign ad. Product studies match reference; label readable where large enough. Photograph believable humans, natural hands, sensory material detail. White flowers/ingredients optional secondary references, not decorative overload. Sophisticated light should arise from each atmosphere: inviting facial modeling, tactile lively still life, enveloping relaxed evening. Preserve richness without glossy sugary blanket finish. Under each column label PALETTE and KEY ELEMENTS. Footer exact 'FRAGRANCE DNA' / 'Top: Cinnamon, Cardamom, Ginger' / 'Heart: Praline, Candied Fruits, White Flowers' / 'Base: Coffee, Vanilla, Tonka Bean, Benzoin, Musk'. No alcohol assumption or performance claims, no extra headlines, no misspelled text.

sources.text:
# Creative Territory Method — Go Natural

Version 4.1 · 2026-11-04 · A guide to exploration, not a checklist.

## Start with the fragrance, then follow promising associations

Start by opening the relevant product section in [fragrance-briefs.md](fragrance-briefs.md): read the collected notes, full brand description, source cautions and previous creative explorations. For a range comparison, read each fragrance’s section side by side. Use [project-brief.md](project-brief.md) for task context and the user’s latest request for current scope. Product photos establish appearance; earlier boards offer creative possibilities. Neither replaces the collected product brief.

Briefly identify the product source used and the specific scent/description cues informing the proposal, so the connection is visible. Then explore freely; collected interpretations are starting points, not permanent assignments. Look at related successful ideas before starting over. Explore through any of these entry points; combine them freely:

| Entry point | What it can open up |
|---|---|
| Ingredient / food | Appetite, pouring, breaking, melting, sensory transformation |
| Material / texture | Silk, powder, grain, softness, weight, physical sensation |
| Place / atmosphere | Escape, an intimate room, a gathering, a particular environment |
| Person / presence | Gesture, attitude, attraction, a way of occupying space |
| Ritual / experience | Getting ready, lingering, gifting, a private or shared moment |
| Concept / contrast | Raw/refined, delicate/powerful, a trace of something invisible |

These are alternative starting points, not stages to complete or categories to allocate. The same fragrance can support several routes; different fragrances can share ingredients and materials. Distinction comes from emphasis, combinations and treatment. How the wearer wants to feel, be perceived or spend a moment can help when relevant.

One more source worth checking before inventing a persona from scratch: [quiz-mechanics.md](quiz-mechanics.md) has the live site quiz's six result personas verbatim — pre-existing brand voice already shown to real quiz-takers, with reachability stats showing which three or four actually carry most of the real-world weight. Useful as a Person/Presence or Ritual/Experience entry point source, not as a fixed allocation of fragrances to personas.

## Develop the world with the idea

Let setting, materials, light, atmosphere, color and photographic finish develop together. Choose light because of what the idea needs. Warm light can be nuanced; cooler light is not a shortcut to sophistication or reduced sweetness. Lighting differences are useful only when they strengthen the ideas. Use the Lighting DNA Decoder skill when closer analysis would help, rather than copying its checklist into every brief.

Keep sensory richness and several possibilities alive. A strong territory may emerge from a food image, a person or a material without needing a strategic tension or clever mechanism. There is no compulsory prop count, palette, tile count or route quota.

## Show possibilities, then develop the chosen direction

The default territory deliverable is an actual comparative visual moodboard with concise titles, ideas, image references, palettes and key elements as useful. Adapt the presentation to the question: several routes for one fragrance, or related fragrances compared together. Written reasoning supports the board; a single finished advertisement does not replace it.

Review which worlds are compelling, credible and worth developing. Use existing choices and request a selection only when genuinely missing. Take the selected direction into alphaprompt-system.md with the actual product reference and placement requirements. Product briefs supply evidence and history, not a permanent prop assignment.

## Precedents: preserve the ideas, improve the photography

Before related vanilla work, inspect the earlier boards in [copy/vanilla world](../copy/vanilla%20world/):

- [Original comparison](../copy/vanilla%20world/Go%20Natural%20Vanilla%20Fragrance%20Moodboard.png): different ingredients, emotions, atmosphere and routes coexist within each fragrance.
- [Madagascar — The Escape](../copy/vanilla%20world/madagascar_vanilla_territory_moodboard.png): lushness, movement, appetite and escape.
- [Crème — The Comfort](../copy/vanilla%20world/vanilla_creme_territory_moodboard.png): cream, almond, tactile softness and ritual.
- [Era — The Second Skin](../copy/vanilla%20world/vanilla_era_territory_moodboard.png): personal presence, fluid fabric, gesture and shadow.
- [Bourbon exploration](../copy/vanilla%20world/8e62dbb1-4375-42ca-af9b-18096037c2c2.png): several interpretations of warmth and depth remain open.

The user values their ideas; their execution can feel generic or overly synthetic. They are conceptual precedents, not approved photographic or layout standards. Preserve the imaginative associations while seeking more specific, believable, intentional image-making. Polish, dramatic light, saturation or ingredient macros are not faults in themselves; judge their effect in context.

Before presenting, compare with the relevant precedents: has the work gained meaning and interest, or merely become more orderly? Assess conceptual strength and visual execution separately. Improve weak rendering without stripping away the idea.

## Keep only the necessary boundaries

Preserve actual product identity; distinguish sourced information from interpretation; meet the requested deliverable and task constraints. Relevant source conflicts belong in fragrance-briefs.md. Detailed research belongs in research-intelligence.md. Respect any agreed generation-cost conditions without inventing a price.

Feedback on an execution stays specific to that execution unless the user makes it broader. “This croissant dominates this image” does not become a ban on food-led exploration. Longer cautions and prior methods are retained under reference/ as historical aids, not extra operating rules.

# Brand Voice — Go Natural

Updated 2026-11-04. Working pitch guidance, not a client-approved final voice system.

## Purpose

Help people imagine the fragrance and encounter a recognizable Go Natural attitude. The precise masterbrand point of view remains open; do not declare memory, identity or personalization unique without comparative evidence.

## Principles

Be concrete, sensorial, confident and specific. Warmth, wit, intimacy and seriousness can vary with product and context while wording remains clear and intentional. Premium does not require distant language, muted personality or stacked luxury adjectives.

For product copy, use whichever layers help:
1. What it smells like: accurate scent character and relevant notes.
2. The physical/sensory experience it evokes.
3. A plausible emotional reward.
4. A possible occasion or social impression.

Not every description needs all four. Metaphor and ingredient information can coexist. “Second skin” can express intimacy; it does not establish low projection. Do not promise unverified performance or guaranteed emotional/social outcomes.

## Existing voice is evidence, not a template to obey blindly

The prior audit records classic sensual descriptions on some core products and casual, emoji-heavy language on newer lines. This is a consistency question, not proof that two registers can never coexist. Explore a shared attitude and context-sensitive expression before deciding whether to standardize, edit or retain differences.

“Architectural restraint meets sensory abundance” is an earlier proposal, not an approved universal voice. Existing quotations and tone examples remain in the archived file.

## Claims and source handling

Use fragrance-briefs.md for notes and source conflicts, brand-dna.md for brand evidence status and research-intelligence.md for reported research. Do not duplicate note pyramids here. Museum retail presence and a formally worded partnership claim are different; use the evidence boundary in Brand DNA. Describe actual personalization/Fragrance Bar services without implying unique capabilities or bespoke perfumery that have not been established.

Avoid automatic tourist symbolism and generic superlatives. Egyptian references can be contemporary and specific where researched. Headlines and typographic overlays are choices for the deliverable, not mandatory lifestyle treatment.

## Review

Does the copy make the smell or experience more imaginable? Does the attitude fit the proposed brand world? Are claims supportable? Is it specific enough to be useful rather than interchangeable praise?

Historical source quotations and the earlier voice audit are retained under reference/workflow-before-cleanup-2026-11-04/brand-voice.md.

# Lifestyle Pillar Exercises — Optional Reference

Updated 2026-11-04. Supporting exercises for creative-territory-method.md; this is not a second mandatory workflow.

## Use when routes feel repetitive

Try any useful starting point:
- Read notes as textures, temperatures or contrasts.
- Look for actions in product language: escape, linger, draw closer, stand out.
- Explore a person, gesture, relationship, ritual or occasion.
- Test a place, material, cultural association or conceptual transformation.

Move among these freely. Ingredients need not come before emotion; props need not determine the idea. Keep a credible product connection and label creative interpretation. Do not infer projection or longevity from copy. Day/night and home/away are possible contexts, not compulsory classifications.

## Useful examples and corrections

- **Three vanillas:** the prior work used Madagascar Vanilla as Escape, Vanilla Crème as Stillness/Comfort and Vanilla Era as Presence/Second Skin. These are creative readings, not permanent product identities. Compare routes visually rather than assign one mandatory world forever.
- **Carmina:** a leather/vetiver-led dark first pass was later revised warmer to reflect the broader description. The rejected light-to-shadow image remains history, not a calibration target. A feminine description does not logically exclude woody notes or dark photography.
- **Bourbon Vanilla:** the name does not imply whiskey. The documented notes include vanilla, tonka, brown sugar, amberwood, musk and patchouli. The earlier barrel/bar image is an experiment with an unsupported name-based rationale; it is not the default. A future bar route needs an independent creative reason.
- **Literal ingredients:** coffee, custard, flowers and coconut can all be useful. Check whether they express the fragrance or accidentally advertise another category.
- **Velvet / Art Deco / Golden Aura:** fabric, geometry and light are candidate interpretations of names, not the only legitimate routes.

## Overlap

If routes look similar, explore a different human situation or visual treatment before claiming product redundancy. Similar notes, objects or copy alone cannot establish that fragrances are commercially redundant. That needs product/customer evidence.

## Historical work

The original method records generations under copy/go-natural-dark-woody-pillars-2026-11-03/, copy/go-natural-carmina-pillars-2026-11-03/ and copy/go-natural-three-vanillas-round2-2026-11-03/. Preserve paths and outcomes as project history; generated does not mean approved or effective. The unabridged method is archived under reference/workflow-before-cleanup-2026-11-04/lifestyle-pillar-method.md.

Terminology reference: [Nielsen-Massey FAQ](https://nielsenmassey.com/faq/), accessed 2026-11-04, explains Bourbon vanilla as geographic rather than whiskey terminology. This does not establish Go Natural's naming intent or ingredient provenance.

# Audience Hypotheses — Go Natural

Updated 2026-11-04. These are exploratory audience lenses, not validated segments, a ranking of market opportunity or proof of what current buyers fear. The original detailed cards are archived under reference/workflow-before-cleanup-2026-11-04/icp-cards.md. Their illustrative quotations are invented research prompts, not customer testimony.

## Personal-meaning seeker

Possible task: buy a fragrance or gift for a meaningful event or relationship. Explore keepsake value, gifting, engraving, perceived quality and whether personalization feels meaningful. Do not assume competitors lack these capabilities.

## Gourmand enthusiast

Possible task: enjoy sweet, warm or creamy scents and explore new variations. Investigate pleasure, sensory preferences, switching, price and continuity with familiar products. Earlier claims that this group fears a cold premium repositioning were hypotheses, not observed objections.

## Contemporary Egyptian brand seeker

Possible task: choose a local brand with contemporary design and cultural relevance. Investigate whether provenance matters, how people recognize it and what they find desirable. Do not assume every buyer rejects heritage imagery or prefers a particular aesthetic.

## How to use

For a brief, identify a plausible person/situation and ask what they want from the scent and from the brand. Internal feeling and social expression may overlap. One person can move among these situations; do not assign fixed personalities from a quiz result. [quiz-mechanics.md](quiz-mechanics.md) has the quiz's actual 6-result scoring system and copy, now verified directly from the live site — useful as brand voice/territory material, not as a replacement for these audience hypotheses.

Use the seven-W/occasion prompts in research-intelligence.md when research warrants it, not as seven mandatory boxes for every moodboard. Validate relevance, frequency, competitor associations and commercial value before making priority-segment or category-entry-point claims.

## Open questions

Who buys, for whom, when and why? What matters in choosing Go Natural over alternatives? Which services create connection? What changes with occasion, budget and familiarity? Existing product breadth and marketing copy suggest questions; they do not answer them.

# Product Formats, Image Treatments and Placements

Updated 2026-11-04. Use relevant guidance only; this file does not choose the creative territory.

## Product formats — what is depicted

- **Full-size perfume:** use the actual SKU reference. State whether packaging is included.
- **Minis/travel/oils/balms:** use the actual format's reference and scale. Do not shrink a full-size bottle or invent a container to represent another format.
- **Gifts/sets/apparel/body/hair:** identify actual contents, packaging and relevant references. Do not transfer EDP notes or claims to a different product without evidence.
- **Experiences:** distinguish conceptual illustration from documentary depiction. Do not invent a venue, collaboration or service capability.

## Image treatments — how it is shown

- **Product hero:** clear product hierarchy. Centered/thirds, background, props, lens and depth follow the selected direction rather than a mandatory gradient or one-prop formula.
- **Flat lay/ingredient study:** overhead when useful, convincing scale/support/contact shadows. Use only relevant ingredients or explicitly interpreted materials; no mandatory count. Conceptual floating imagery is possible if deliberately selected, not an accidental realism failure.
- **Lifestyle/environment:** setting and action come from the selected board. A neutral or colorful treatment can work; relevance and hierarchy matter.
- **Wearer:** gesture, distance and social presence according to the idea. Candid/posed, crop and wardrobe are task choices. Do not add forced foreground clutter, jewelry or a patterned cuff to manufacture authenticity.
- **Experience:** ritual, discovery, engraving, presentation and gifting where supported. Ceremonial framing is valid. Verify partner/venue claims before public use.

## Placements — where it appears

- **Website hero/banner:** use actual placement dimensions, crop needs, legibility and text space.
- **Product-page imagery:** clarify product/format; use an informative image sequence.
- **Social carousel:** set ratio and sequence for the story. The earlier Nayomi 4:5, 1080×1350 example is an option, not a universal five-slide narrative or generation-endpoint requirement.
- **Comparative moodboard:** follow creative-territory-method.md. Its collages, headings and palette swatches are exploratory presentation, not one campaign frame. Use a readable layout such as the supplied landscape three-column reference.

## Task-specific constraints

Record ratio, packaging inclusion, subject/wardrobe requirements, copy, number of outputs and technical delivery needs in the current brief. Bottle only / no packaging / 4:3 applies when the task specifies it. Avoid unsupported third-party names or marks in public creative; an accurately identified research/reference image is a different use.

Use credible materials, lighting and geometry as appropriate to the chosen medium. Detailed realism prompting is owned by alphaprompt-system.md, not an extra mandatory layer checklist here.

sources.text:
# AlphaPrompt — Execution System

Updated 2026-11-04. Translate a selected creative direction into an image prompt. Use creative-territory-method.md when the task is still exploration or a comparative moodboard.

## Inputs

Read the current task in project-brief.md, the selected moodboard/direction, the relevant product evidence in fragrance-briefs.md, the actual reference image and relevant guidance in product-type-briefs.md. Brand expression follows visual-direction.md and brand-voice.md.

The selected board supplies the scene, styling and photographic direction. The fragrance brief supplies facts, source conflicts and previous work; its earlier props are not compulsory. If a consequential decision is missing, resolve that decision rather than reinventing the whole brief.

## Five-part prompt

1. **Reference Lock:** identify the actual product reference; preserve bottle proportions, cap material/color, liquid, label artwork, logo and typography. Do not copy reflected background marks as permanent product details. Do not silently repair real packaging inconsistencies.
2. **Scene & Action:** express the selected idea through environment, action and relevant elements. Give each element a role.
3. **Composition:** placement, framing, scale, camera perspective, depth, crop, aspect ratio and useful negative space.
4. **Aesthetic Engine:** specify the photographic treatment that serves this scene: light source/direction/quality, shadow, color, reflections, texture and retouching. Hard and soft treatments are both possible; protect required label legibility.
5. **Constraints:** state task-specific inclusions/exclusions and the identity locks. Keep them short, concrete and relevant.

## Realism guidance

Use credible materials, weight, support, perspective and reflections. Specify texture or natural variation where it helps; there is no requirement to invent one imperfection for every object. Include camera/subject behavior/environment detail when relevant. Candid, ceremonial and studio treatments are all available; foreground clutter is optional, not proof of realism.

Prop count, architecture, surfaces, palette and lighting follow the selected direction and placement. There are no blanket bans on stone, beige, hard shadows or literal ingredients. Avoid unmotivated clichés and visual competition, not entire categories of artistic choices. Product accuracy remains mandatory when showing a real SKU.

## Before generation

Confirm the requested deliverable, product reference, source choice for any disputed claim, selected direction and task constraints. For a reference-free atmosphere study, do not invent a real branded bottle. For a comparative board, use the board specification in creative-territory-method.md rather than one final-image composition.

Respect any explicitly agreed generation quote/confirmation requirement. Never invent a tool price or treat confirmation as a way to re-ask already answered creative questions. A direct generation request within an agreed scope authorizes that creative task; it does not imply approval of unquoted external charges.

## Review

Check concept communication, identity/text accuracy, hierarchy, physical/material plausibility and brief compliance. Compare a series for coherent intent and recognition rather than identical light or a fixed number of props. Fix the relevant failure, preserving successful choices.

## History

Earlier reflection-copying, plastic flowers, floating ingredients and Carmina styling failures remain useful lessons. Their detailed records are under reference/workflow-before-cleanup-2026-11-04/alphaprompt-system.md and lifestyle-pillar-method.md. Historical failures are not universal aesthetic prohibitions.

# Fragrance Briefs — Evidence and Creative History

Updated 2026-11-04. These records separate sourced information from candidate worlds. Notes and descriptions are carried from earlier project sources and were not externally reverified during cleanup. “Recorded agreement” is the prior audit status, not a fresh verification.

Use the actual product reference for identity, the selected moodboard for the current direction, and product-type-briefs.md for format/placement. No fragrance is permanently locked to one prop world, gendered aesthetic, intensity or time of day. A generated image is a test, not proof of effectiveness or approval.

Full earlier quotations, detailed generation paths and historical variants are preserved in reference/workflow-before-cleanup-2026-11-04/fragrance-briefs.md. They are history, not additional instructions. The actual catalog snapshots remain source records; reconcile dates and versions for final claims.

## Caramel Latte

**Recorded notes source:** Website.

**Notes:** Caramel/Milk → Honey/White Flowers → Vanilla/Musk

**Recorded brand description:** “If you love the smell of a creamy lactonic vanilla ice cream drenched in honey and caramel, this is undoubtedly your ultimate perfume! With a longevity of 10 out of 10, this fragrance persists. oh and yes you will smell edible!”

**Source status / cautions:** Earlier label audit flags top-note wording differences (condensed milk/sugar). Retain the source choice; do not describe the whole record as conflict-free.

**Creative history / options:** Café/barista ritual; historical generated route, not required.

**Previously recorded reference/history paths:** `products/Caramel_Latte.webp`. Check the actual files before use.

## Crème Brûlée

**Recorded notes source:** Label/website records.

**Notes:** Caramel/Milk/Sugar → Honey/White Flowers → Vanilla/Praline/Musk

**Recorded brand description:** “This is a sweet, rich, creamy, milky vanilla fragrance, like a caramel sundae, with warm, sticky caramel on thick, creamy, vanilla ice cream.”

**Source status / cautions:** Earlier workbook and website snapshots differ in level of note detail. Retain versions and source dates.

**Creative history / options:** Restaurant finale, brittle sugar/soft custard; historical generated route.

## Salted Caramel

**Recorded notes source:** Label record plus website description.

**Notes:** Pistachio/Almond → Heliotrope/Jasmine → Caramel/Vanilla/Salt/Sandalwood

**Recorded brand description:** “Deliciously addictive, creamy pistachio, rich salted caramel, and warm vanilla blend like a perfect summer memory. It's sunshine, sweetness, and all-day compliments because who doesn't love Salted Caramel?!”

**Source status / cautions:** No independently reverified current pyramid in this cleanup.

**Creative history / options:** Candy-shop/summer nostalgia; historical generated route.

## Talya

**Recorded notes source:** Label record; description in catalog.

**Notes:** Pink Pepper → Gourmand accord → Musk/Vanilla

**Recorded brand description:** “Imagine a creamy, soft and powdery milkshake with a delightful hint of berries, vanilla and musk. It's flirtatiously sweet, but not too sweet!”

**Source status / cautions:** The prior brief called the pyramid label-only, but the catalog export also records these notes. No new current-site check.

**Creative history / options:** Soda-fountain/milkshake texture; historical generated route.

## Madagascar Vanilla

**Recorded notes source:** Recorded label/website agreement.

**Notes:** Jasmine/Gardenia/Croissant → Whipped Cream/Brown Sugar/Tonka → Madagascar Vanilla/Coconut

**Recorded brand description:** “This sophisticated scent combines creamy Coconut, crisp Croissant, and warm Madagascar Vanilla for an utterly addictive island escape. The result is a deliciously exotic yet subtly sweet fragrance that is sure to captivate and delight. Enjoy a tropical getaway with each spritz of this sensuous and inviting aroma.”

**Source status / cautions:** Actual product reference was supplied in this chat. No note conflict recorded here.

**Creative history / options:** Earlier Escape reading and new comparative board: Somewhere Else / Nothing Urgent / Soft Landing. Somewhere Else was selected for an initial test; later clarification established the comparative board as the intended territory deliverable. No blanket approval of every tile.

**Previously recorded reference/history paths:** `products/Madagascar_Vanilla.webp`, `_flat_lay.webp`. Check the actual files before use.

## Vanilla Crème

**Recorded notes source:** Label and website records.

**Notes:** Crème → Almond (website adds Milk) → Creamy Vanilla/Skin Musk/Tonka

**Recorded brand description:** “This soft, creamy vanilla fragrance is like wearing a warm, powdery, fluffy cloud. It's a 10/10 for anyone who wants to smell like a dream!”

**Source status / cautions:** Minor source wording variance retained; not silently normalized. Distinguish EDP from similarly named oil.

**Creative history / options:** Cloud/stone route overlapped with Vanilla Era. The prior round-2 custard route was preferred in that test. Comfort/Stillness is a creative reading, not a required food scene.

## Vanilla Era

**Recorded notes source:** Recorded label/reference and brand description.

**Notes:** Vanilla Orchid/Sugar → Jasmine Blossom/White Flowers → Tonka/Agarwood/Vanilla

**Recorded brand description:** “A scent that feels like second skin—soft, warm, and effortlessly seductive. Creamy sugary vanilla bean melts into delicate white florals, creating an intoxicating sweetness that lingers like a secret only you know. Velvety Agar wood and Tonka wrap around you, leaving a trail that feels both comforting and captivating. Vanilla Era is not just a fragrance—it's an experience: timeless, luxurious, and impossible to forget.”

**Source status / cautions:** “Second skin” and “all-day” are brand language, not measured low projection or proof of universal occasion fit.

**Creative history / options:** Presence/Second Skin, fabric/proximity; historical generated interpretation. Hard surfaces or glossy elements are not categorically forbidden.

**Previously recorded reference/history paths:** `products/Vanilla_Era.jpg`. Check the actual files before use.

## Golden Aura

**Recorded notes source:** Label record and website description.

**Notes:** Vanilla/Lavender/Cacao/Ginger → Vanilla Caviar → Vanilla Absolute

**Recorded brand description:** “Meet Golden Aura a creamy vanilla, cozy lavender, and a touch of woodiness. It's confidence in a bottle with a glow-up vibe. Smell golden, feel unstoppable!”

**Source status / cautions:** Notes source is the recorded label, not inferred from the shorter descriptive copy.

**Creative history / options:** Glowing confidence/light-led route; no generation recorded in prior brief.

## Caribbean Coconut

**Recorded notes source:** Label record and website description.

**Notes:** Coconut/Ylang-Ylang → Almond Blossom/Sambac Jasmine/Toasted Coconut → Vanilla Cream/Velvet/White Musk/Tonka

**Recorded brand description:** “This luxurious Caribbean Coconut Eau De Perfume is a must-have for any coconut lover looking for a unique and exotic scent! With its exotic yet delicate notes of coconut, jasmine and vanilla, it's the perfect way to stay smelling like a tropical vacation all day long. The soft and luxurious undertones will make you feel like you're in paradise no matter where you go!”

**Source status / cautions:** “Velvet” is recorded descriptive note wording; it is not a literal ingredient provenance claim.

**Creative history / options:** Freedom/Delight and resort textures; proposed, not a mandatory beach setting.

## Juliette

**Recorded notes source:** Conflicting label and website records.

**Notes:** Label: Peach/Patchouli/Orange → Caramel/Whipped Cream/Orange Blossom/Ruby Jasmine → Heliotrope/Sandalwood/Cashmere Wood/Amber/Cedar. Website: Gunpowder/Patchouli/Bergamot → Caramel/Whipped Cream/Vanilla/Marshmallow/Benzoin → Cotton Candy/Caramel/Cashmere Wood/Raspberry/Tonka.

**Recorded brand description:** “Juliette is an irresistibly sexy, sensual and evocative fragrance. It's deeper, fuller and heavier than other perfumes, embodying what we can only describe as a sweet scent grown up. The key to its alluring scent is the irresistible caramel notes, aiming to evoke the feeling and absolute pursuit of pure pleasure. Wear it on a date and you'll be sure to turn heads!”

**Source status / cautions:** UNRESOLVED. State the chosen source for exploratory use; verify current version before final factual copy. Do not average the pyramids. Cashmere fabric is a metaphorical styling association, not a literal ingredient established by “cashmere wood.”

**Creative history / options:** Grown-up sweetness, Desire/Tenderness, date context from quoted brand language; historical tests. Performance remains a brand claim.

**Previously recorded reference/history paths:** `products/Juliette.webp`, `download_*.webp`. Check the actual files before use.

## Tipsy

**Recorded notes source:** Label record and website description.

**Notes:** Cinnamon/Cardamom/Ginger → Praline/Candied Fruits/White Flowers → Coffee/Vanilla/Tonka/Benzoin/Musk

**Recorded brand description:** “Spicy, sweet, and just a little bit risky—Tipsy is like a cozy night out that you can wear! Cinnamon, praline, and a touch of coffee create a scent that's bold, addictive, and made to make people lean in a little closer. Go ahead, get Tipsy!”

**Source status / cautions:** The recorded description spans nights out and evenings in; no compulsory time/place slot.

**Creative history / options:** Warm spice, coffee or dessert cocktail, knit texture; proposals, not evidence of an alcohol accord.

## Nayomi

**Recorded notes source:** Label record and website description.

**Notes:** Orange Blossom/Neroli/Almond → Jasmine/Apricot/Violet → Musk/Jasmine/Sandalwood

**Recorded brand description:** “Nayomi opens with soft orange blossom, neroli, and almond, blooms into creamy jasmine and apricot, then melts into warm musk and sandalwood. A delicate yet addictive scent made for feminine elegance and everyday luxury. Vibe it gives: Clean but sweet / Soft floral gourmand / 'Smells expensive' energy / **Skin-hugging and comforting**.”

**Source status / cautions:** Preserve exact reference/version; label #4 is also recorded for Madagascar Vanilla. Do not repair numbering silently.

**Creative history / options:** Intimacy/proximity and prior five-slide carousel. Actual non-note props need relevance, not automatic replacement with ingredients.

**Previously recorded reference/history paths:** `ig feed.jpg`, `products/JPEGimage-4BB3-B326-1D-0.webp`, `download_6b7dc460...webp`. Check the actual files before use.

## Velvet Musk

**Recorded notes source:** Recorded structured pyramid.

**Notes:** Peony/Bergamot → Bulgarian Rose/Patchouli → Vanilla/Musk

**Recorded brand description:** “Velvet Musk is a luxurious and sophisticated fragrance that combines velvety musk with a blend of Bulgarian rose and vanilla. Its warm and powerful scent is both delicate and strong, making it perfect for any occasion. Top notes are peony and bergamot; middle notes are Bulgarian rose and patchouli; base notes are vanilla and musk.”

**Source status / cautions:** The structured pyramid is the recorded source choice; distinguish it from loose top/heart wording in brand prose.

**Creative history / options:** Tenderness/Serenity and velvet fabric were earlier proposals. The Invisible Touch is a later conceptual route; no final selection recorded here.

**Previously recorded reference/history paths:** `products/Velvet_Musk.webp`, `download_cc8ee4ec...webp`. Check the actual files before use.

## Carmina

**Recorded notes source:** Label record and brand reception copy.

**Source status / cautions:** No established note conflict merely because copy calls it sweet/feminine/fresh. Gender descriptors do not logically determine family or photographic style.

With soft notes of aloe vera and chamomile, Summer Haze! is ideal for all your Summer night adventures. Spritz on and let the sweet smell of Summer take over!”

**Source status / cautions:** UNRESOLVED base. A suspected copy/print error is not proven. Use agreed notes if needed; do not substitute an inferred aloe-like base as fact.

## Egyptian Oud

**Source status / cautions:** “Magic of Egypt” and “perfect for any occasion” are brand claims, not proof of cultural specificity or performance.

## Bourbon Vanilla

**Recorded notes source:** Recorded label/website sources.

**Notes:** Vanilla Orchid/Jasmine → Brown Sugar/Tonka → Amber/Amberwood/Musk/Patchouli

**Recorded brand description:** “An oriental blend of Madagascar vanilla orchid, Brazilian Tonka, musk, amber, patchouli and brown sugar. It has beautifully balanced oriental notes of musk, amber, patchouli and brown sugar from the distinguished wood base of this utterly sublime scent.”

**Source status / cautions:** Bourbon vanilla is geographic terminology, not evidence of whiskey. No alcohol accord is established by the supplied description. Box #22 / bottle #20 discrepancy remains recorded.

**Creative history / options:** Vanilla warmth/woody-amber depth is a candidate reading. The earlier barrel/bar image remains a historical experiment with a corrected name-based rationale, not a preferred route.

**Previously recorded reference/history paths:** `creative-territory-method.md`, `bourbon-vanilla-barrel.png`, `products/Bourbon_Vanilla.jpg`. Check the actual files before use.

## Art Deco

**Recorded notes source:** Label record and website description.

**Notes:** Cinnamon/Cardamom/Orange Blossom → Vanilla → Musk/Tonka/Almond

**Recorded brand description:** “An enchanting elixir that combines warmth and freshness in a unique blend. With a delightful mix of vanilla, citrus, spices, and rich woods, its layers unfold gradually, harmonizing beautifully to create a captivating scent experience on your skin.”

**Source status / cautions:** Website prose mentions rich woods but the recorded pyramid does not list a wood note. Preserve that distinction. Orange blossom does not establish orange peel as an ingredient. Box #12 / bottle #11 discrepancy recorded.

**Creative history / options:** Geometry and polished/raw contrast are proposals. Raw Ingredients. Refined Geometry is not selected; no generation recorded in prior brief.

**Previously recorded reference/history paths:** `products/Art_Deco.jpg`. Check the actual files before use.

## Signature

**Recorded notes source:** Label record and brand language.

**Notes:** Indian Saffron/Cinnamon/Orange → Caramel/Amber/Rosemary → Tonka Bean/Vanilla

**Source status / cautions:** Brand phrases “cozy evening, soft candlelight, effortless elegance” and “warm luxury and quiet confidence” guide interpretation; no measured intensity is established.

**Creative history / options:** Quiet confidence/candlelit warmth; proposal, no generation recorded in prior brief.

## Legacy

**Recorded notes source:** Label and website records.

**Notes:** Label: Lavender/Mandarin Orange/Black Currant/Petitgrain → Lavender/Orange Blossom/Jasmine → Madagascar Vanilla/Musk/Cedar/Ambergris. Website prose mentions Lavender/Bergamot and Orange Blossom/Jasmine.

**Recorded brand description:** “...combination of floral and spicy notes, it's a daring scent of freedom which produces a unique and captivating aroma. Lavender and bergamot, as the top notes, bring out a fresh scent; whereas orange blossom and jasmine as the heart notes give off a subtle yet sexy fragrance.”

**Source status / cautions:** Bergamot vs the label citrus list is a source variation; do not certify it as identical or resolve it by calling the website simplified.

**Creative history / options:** Freedom/aromatic or apothecary reading; proposal, no generation recorded in prior brief.

## Other formats

Perfume oils recorded in the range include Strawberry ShortCake, Sucré, Belle Époque, White Musk, Vanilla Créam and Baby Powder. The earlier audit flags duplicated note copy between Strawberry ShortCake and vanilla wording; do not resolve the duplication by guesswork. Baby Powder notes occur in the export despite an earlier unavailable flag. Verify the specific product/version.

French Lace, Pillow Talk and Mémoire hair perfumes need their own references and claims; lack of a printed pyramid is not proof no description exists elsewhere. Minis, balms, oils and hair formats are not automatically interchangeable with an EDP brief.

## Bourbon terminology source

[Nielsen-Massey FAQ](https://nielsenmassey.com/faq/), accessed 2026-11-04, explains Bourbon vanilla as geographic rather than whiskey terminology. This does not establish Go Natural's naming intent or ingredient provenance.

sources.text:
# Brand DNA — Go Natural (Egypt)

Updated 2026-11-04. Working intelligence summary for an independent pitch, not approved positioning or a verified present-day brand manual.

## What the project knows and assumes

The prior research records an Egyptian fragrance brand founded in 2017, with website gonaturalegypt.com. The cited creative brief asks for stronger premium perception and coherent website imagery. “Premium niche” is an aspiration in the brief, not proof of current consumer perception or an adopted strategy.

The previous audit transcribes the brand statement around memories, individuality, elegance, confidence and fragrance as a lasting feeling. The latest research handoff also reports “Enhancing your rare natural beauty,” “Make It Personal” and “A fragrance made yours.” Retain exact sources/dates before using quotations publicly; these are brand expressions, not evidence that consumers perceive differentiation.

The historical catalog and project evidence record perfumes, travel formats, oils, balms, body/hair products, gifting and scent-linked apparel, plus engraving and Fragrance Bar events. Availability, pricing, catalog counts and exact service mechanics need date-specific checking. Do not describe Fragrance Bar as bespoke perfumery or expert one-to-one consultation without evidence.

## Existing capabilities are not automatically differentiation

Discovery, personalization, layering and gifting are useful capabilities. Their uniqueness or commercial advantage has not been established. Earlier claims of unique personalization and experiences absent from competitors are withdrawn pending comparative evidence.

research-intelligence.md preserves the new competitor/quiz/industry handoffs. They report Nspired's value attitude, Nuit's emotional and cross-format offers, Breathe's performance/value claims and Siwa's choice/discovery model. These are reported expressed positions, not measured consumer associations; source verification belongs in the research layer. Earlier comparisons with Frag, Hathor, Soul & More and other adjacent brands remain in the archived audit as leads rather than permanent ownership claims.

## Brand meaning versus product meaning

Product storytelling should help a person imagine the actual scent and relevant experience. Masterbrand development should answer why someone would want that experience from Go Natural.

Use internal reward, desired social impression and occasion as optional lenses. They are not validated customer segments. A fragrance wardrobe as “ways to feel and ways to show up” is a working strategic hypothesis, not a selected positioning or an uncontested competitive space.

Open routes include fragrance styling/wardrobe curation, greater customer participation, contemporary Egyptian fragrance creativity and different expressions of self. They may operate at different levels: positioning, service, portfolio architecture or campaign platform. Do not collapse them into a slogan before testing credibility and difference.

## Evidence corrections and unresolved items

- **Museum presence:** the prior audit records photographs of retail presence in the Grand Egyptian Museum. Preserve that observation; check original images, current status and exact relationship wording before a public partnership claim. The older “unverified collaboration” instruction is superseded by this narrower distinction.
- **Heat Sticks:** the later audit identifies the campaign as an April 1 stunt, not an ongoing product line. The earlier real-SKU warning is superseded. Keep it as a reported playful campaign example, with original source verification before client-facing use.
- **Juliette:** packaging and website note descriptions differ in the recorded sources. Neither should silently overwrite the other. fragrance-briefs.md owns the conflict and task-specific source choice.
- **Carmina:** the recorded label notes and broad reception copy are different types of information, not an established note conflict. Keep the warmer creative correction as history; do not infer scent-family eligibility from gender language.
- **Summer Haze / Muhra:** preserve unresolved note-source versions in fragrance-briefs.md; do not turn an inferred “likely misprint” into a corrected fact.
- **Chat concierge:** an answer is a dated brand-system output to check against original product evidence, not inherently the most accurate source.
- **Counts/taxonomies:** separate official site navigation, research scent families and creative emotional readings. Snapshot product listings, named-range records and variants are different units.
- **Premium perception:** prior criticisms of sales badges, ratings and shipping banners were interpretations. Those elements alone do not establish that a brand is not premium. Evaluate presentation and customer response rather than assert a universal retail rule.

## Visual and verbal implications

A masterbrand can be recognizable across gourmand, fresh, woody, intimate, playful, masculine and feminine expressions. Candidate constants include typography, layout, product treatment, copy principles or repeatable devices; none should be presented as approved merely because it appears on a moodboard.

Premiumization may involve clearer attitude, curation, sensory specificity, quality image-making and coherent experiences. It does not prescribe one palette, lighting setup or voice. Contemporary Egyptian specificity should emerge from credible evidence, not automatic tourist imagery or an assumption that layering is a new imported behavior.

## Quiz mechanics — now verified

[quiz-mechanics.md](quiz-mechanics.md) replaces the earlier "reported, not inspected" quiz note with the live scoring logic, all 6 question/option/scoring tables, the 6 result profiles verbatim, and a stats run across every possible answer path. Headline finding: the 6 named results are not evenly reachable — bold, floral and musk together account for ~77% of possible outcomes, vanilla ~18%, and caramel/sweet are long-tail (under 5% combined, with "La Chérie" reachable by only 2 of 4,096 possible paths). This is a structural property of the scoring code, not evidence of real customer answer patterns, which remain unknown. Treat the six names as an existing brand asset worth drawing on for territory language, not as a validated segmentation model — see icp-cards.md's caution on this.

## Next research decisions

Identify relevant buying/usage situations; examine Egyptian fragrance practices; compare actual competitor services; distinguish customization from felt connection; test recognition, desirability and proposed premium perception; determine whether real quiz-takers' answers actually cluster the way the structural reachability stats suggest. Creative exploration can continue while these remain open.

## Source trail

Detailed handoffs are preserved in research-intelligence.md with reported-evidence status. Original brand-folder wording, source quotations, prices, partner/event leads and historical corrections are retained under reference/workflow-before-cleanup-2026-11-04/brand-dna.md. Use those as research history, not extra active instructions. Product sources live in the existing catalog snapshots and fragrance briefs; they were not externally reverified during this documentation cleanup.

territories.idea: Anticipation becomes pleasure. Food/sensation route: creamy folds, slow melt and a small indulgence.

territories.notes: Recorded creative history in fragrance-briefs.md. Earlier selection was for an initial test only; comparative board remains missing. Not a universal approval.
